boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Peachtree Creek record (July 20, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. Hood replaced Johnston on July 17-18; the Union crossings of July 19 and McPherson's approach on the east the same day are context. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the Army of the Cumberland and the Army of Tennessee without counts; the live field reads zero. Hood gives the army's effective strength when he took command on July 18 as 33,750 infantry, 3,500 artillery and 10,000 cavalry, with 1,500 Georgia militia, a total of 48,750. Cox's Appendix A gives Johnston's July 10 return (present 73,849, effectives 50,932). Cox calls the Army of the Cumberland nearly fifty thousand men, says Hood's attack fell on Newton's division and Hooker's corps while Palmer's corps was almost unemployed, and gives Hardee's formation of four divisions with Cleburne's in reserve.
claims.rationale: Army totals on different dates and bases (effective, present) and an approximate Union army size; none measures the troops engaged and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Hood says his object was to crush Thomas's army before it could fortify and then turn on Schofield and McPherson, attacking at 1 p.m. by divisions in echelon from the right. Cox says Hood and his subordinates meant a decisive engagement, and cites Johnston's statement that he had told Hood of his plan to attack at Peachtree Creek. NPS says Johnston had decided to attack Thomas before being relieved.
claims.rationale: Stated plans from interested accounts and a summary; not a causal estimate.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Hood says Stewart's corps carried temporary works but had to abandon them, and that when the attack failed he withdrew the troops to their former positions. Cox says the attack was repulsed along the whole line. NPS says the Union troops held and the Confederates fell back.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 6,506 (US 1,710; CS 4,796). Cox gives the Army of the Cumberland's reported loss, except Palmer's corps, as 1,707; notes that Hood did not dispute Hooker's estimate of 4,400 Confederate killed and wounded in front of the Twentieth Corps; says Geary's parties buried 409 Confederates; puts the Confederate dead at not below 800 and total losses at about six thousand. Hood's report gives no figure for the day.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Cox's Confederate figures are estimates built on burial counts and an assumed ratio; Cox's 1,707 excludes Palmer's corps and differs from the frozen 1,710.

open_questions: Thomas's, Hooker's, Newton's, Geary's, Ward's and Williams's reports, Stewart's and Hardee's accounts of July 20 (Hardee's report was read for GA022 but is not a family here) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Hood's February 15, 1865 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, is a third family (interested Confederate account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
